hints: A hash set answers `has` instantly and cannot answer `startsWith` without looking at every word. What structure shares the work between words with the same beginning?
A tree whose edges are letters: the path from the root spells a prefix, and every word that begins with it lives below that node.
So both questions are the same walk down from the root, one letter at a time. They differ only in what is asked at the end.
`startsWith` succeeds if the walk gets there at all; `has` needs the node to be marked as the end of a word, which is the one extra bit each node carries.
